description: The default lane: a stock compressed-tensors checkpoint that vanilla vLLM serves with no forked runtime and no custom kernels. This is the only lane whose correctness depends on nothing we maintain, which is why it is the default even where CB wins the matched-byte accuracy pair.
wired_architectures_note: The default lane: `*` means every registered model profile, because every architecture ships through compressed-tensors (`DEFAULT_EXPORT_LANE`) and enumerating them here would be a second roster to keep in step with model_profiles/registry.py. A NON-default lane names its architectures explicitly.

served_activation_quantization.rationale: DERIVED, not asserted (principle 14). vLLM has no packaged runtime_contract.json, but on this lane the executed activation contract is a FUNCTION OF THE ARTIFACT WE WRITE: vLLM's compressed-tensors dispatcher selects the scheme from the checkpoint's own `config_groups[*].input_activations`, which `export_native_compressed` emits from its per-format scheme table. So the two ends of the chain are both readable, and this list is their intersection rather than a belief about a runtime. Verified against the image the `serve` block names (gridbook:0.8.6-clean-dde15e0) AND the current serving pin (gridbook:0.8.10-clean-f4b3274): both ship the byte-identical vLLM build 0.26.1rc1.dev693+g7f7a32cfe.d20260812, same call sites at the same line numbers. Per format, producer field -> consumer predicate -> executed kernel: (1) NVFP4 -- NVFP4_SCHEME.input_activations num_bits=4 group_size=16 dynamic='local' (export_native_compressed.py:7095) selects CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4(use_a16=False); dense runs kernels/linear/nvfp4/cutlass.py:56 `scaled_fp4_quant(x, layer.input_global_scale_inv)` into `cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm`, and the fused-MoE path sets `activation_key=None if use_a16 else kNvfp4Dynamic` (compressed_tensors_moe_w4a4_nvfp4.py:60). Real A4 on BOTH the dense and the packed-expert route -- checked separately, because one lane answering differently per family is exactly what the CB lane got wrong on 2026-08-17. (2) FP8_E4M3 (the FP8_DYNAMIC menu alias, format_registry.py:190) -- FP8_E4M3_SCHEME.input_activations strategy='token' dynamic=True (export_native_compressed.py:7171) selects the W8A8 FP8 scheme; the MoE route builds `make_fp8_moe_quant_config(..., per_act_token_quant=is_per_token)` (compressed_tensors_moe_w8a8_fp8.py:352). Real A8. (3) MXFP8_E4M3 / MXFP8_E5M2 -- MXFP8_SCHEME.input_activations num_bits=8 group_size=32 dynamic=True; CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8 documents 'Activations are dynamically quantized to MXFP8 at runtime'. Real A8. Listed even though MXFP8 is de-menued for inference, because this field describes the LANE, not one run's menu. (4) FP8_SOURCE -- FP8_SOURCE_SCHEME.input_activations strategy='tensor' dynamic=True (export_native_compressed.py:7158), so the runtime does execute a per-tensor dynamic A8. It is listed for that reason, but see `known_hole` below: no A-side is priced for it today. ABSENT ON PURPOSE: MXFP4 -- MXFP4_SCHEME declares NO `input_activations` key at all (export_native_compressed.py:7121), so vLLM sees a weight-only group and serves it W4A16. The format registry's descriptor says quantizes_activations=True, so pricing MXFP4 off the registry would charge a phantom A4 to a rung this lane serves at A16 -- the exact shape of the DSv4 mispricing. The registry is not the authority here; this list is. BF16 -- ships as plain bf16 on the checkpoint's ignore list, no config_group, no scheme. NVFP4A16/MXFP8A16/INT8_W8A16/INT4_W4A16_g128/FP8_E5M2 -- not in export_native_compressed.EXPORTABLE_FORMATS, so they cannot reach this lane at all.
served_activation_quantization.known_hole: FP8_SOURCE is listed as executed but is priced at zero regardless, because its FormatDescriptor carries quantizes_activations=False and aqua_activation_cost skips non-activation formats BEFORE consulting this list (aqua_activation_cost.py:479). That is a hole, not a measured zero. It is listed rather than omitted so that flipping the descriptor starts pricing it automatically instead of silently keeping a zero. SCOPE (principle 14 corollary): no artifact shipped on this lane has combined an FP8_SOURCE rung with an AQUA-priced cost, so this hole has never affected a shipped allocation. The first run that puts FP8_SOURCE on the menu WITH AQUA must resolve it first.
served_activation_quantization.why_this_matters: This list is what prices the NVFP4-vs-FP8 split on the default lane, and the two rungs differ by an A4-vs-A8 activation error on top of their weight error. Getting it wrong is not conservative in either direction: charging a phantom A-side buys weight bits to escape a cost the runtime never incurs (the DSv4 92 GB body moved 96.8% nvfp4_cb -> 25.4% FP8_CB under exactly that error), while omitting a real one sells 4-bit rungs at a discount, which is the blindness AQUA exists to remove. Unlike the CB lane there is no serve-side `emit_route` telemetry here to catch a mistake after the fact, so the producer-side derivation above is the only check -- which is why every claim cites both the field we write and the predicate that reads it.
served_activation_quantization.if_this_changes: Re-derive; do not edit by hand and never edit to silence a refusal. The chain has exactly two moving parts: (a) export_native_compressed's per-format scheme table -- if a scheme gains or loses `input_activations`, this list changes with it, and MXFP4 is the live example of a format one field away from flipping; (b) the pinned vLLM build in the serve image -- re-grep the dense kernel and the fused-MoE method SEPARATELY, since they are different code paths and a family can change alone. A stronger version of this entry would be a preflight that reads the emitted quantization_config and asserts this list equals the set of config_groups carrying `input_activations`; that is the natural next step and would make the derivation mechanical rather than cited.

gates.description: vLLM eager load + greedy generate on the exported artifact.
Same, with CUDA-graph capture on (a format may load eager and fail capture).
PPL + p99 per-prompt NLL + coherence against a running serve. p99 exists because a broken 27B once passed on the mean while 80% of prompts were broken.
Exact full-vocab vLLM KL-vs-BF16 on WikiText, served artifact, matched bpp (n=8 x seqlen=512). The gold metric; manual by design.
Direct WikiText PPL on the served artifact. Must be a NO-spec-decode serve: echo+logprobs returns the draft model's NLL.

kl_evaluator.note: Resident held-out KL over Pareto assignments, production-cache rendered; feeds select_validated_frontier. Returns (mean, per_sequence, stats) with kl_p95/kl_p99/kl_max/nll_p99 (R9).

notes: Nothing in run-pipeline.sh blocks on a quality number on ANY lane, native included: `vllm` is not importable in the build venv, so the build tool would have to own the serving stack. The shipcard is the refusal contract instead (R13).
Whether these gates become BLOCKING is the open half of R16's verdict and is deferred to Robert.

2026-08-14: the serve image was `vllm-fresh-b12x:latest`, which does NOT exist on this box (CLAUDE.md §7 is stale on it) — corrected to gridbook:0.8.6-clean-dde15e0 (vLLM 0.26.1rc1, compressed-tensors 0.17.0, transformers 5.15.0), verified serving Qwen3.8-27B. Its ENTRYPOINT is nvidia_entrypoint.sh, which passes argv through rather than prepending `vllm serve`, so the command carries `vllm serve` explicitly. The gold.ppl runner was also a dead path: the file is tools/measure_vllm_wikitext_ppl.py.

Both gold runners import vLLM directly (offline LLM API), so they run INSIDE the serving container against the artifact path — they do not talk to the endpoint above. Only ship_gate.ppl_p99nll uses base_url.

2026-08-14: `endpoint.base_url` is the OpenAI API root and is right for a client, but validate_quantized_model's --base-url is the SERVER root (it appends /v1/completions itself and reads /health + /metrics off the root). Passing the /v1 spelling made the gate poll /v1/health (404) for its full 900s timeout without sending one prompt, so the ship_gate runner now spells the root explicitly. run_validation also normalizes a trailing /v1 now, and the spec-decode guard was changed to FAIL CLOSED — it had been swallowing the 404 and returning 'no spec-decode detected', i.e. the guard against publishing the draft model's NLL was issuing a confident all-clear it had no basis for.
